area: Area I. Pilot Privileges and Currency
objective: By the end of this lesson you can read a logbook and say whether the flight review is current and when it runs out, name every event that can take its place (including a WINGS phase), and explain what a good review covers and who may give it.
why: No one may act as pilot in command without a current flight review or something that replaces it. Used well, it is also the one regular check where an instructor looks at how you really fly.

prereading.what: The flight review rule itself: content, the 24 calendar month window, the exceptions, and the simulator option.
prereading.label: 14 CFR 61.56

prereading.what: How the FAA wants a flight review planned, flown, debriefed and recorded.
prereading.label: AC 61-98E Ch 4, 4-1 to 4-8

prereading.what: Sample flight review checklist, pilot interview, Part 91 review guide and sample endorsement.
prereading.label: AC 61-98E App D to F

prereading.what: The WINGS Pilot Proficiency Program: levels, phases, credit and endorsements.
prereading.label: AC 61-91K

prereading.what: Flight reviews from the instructor's side, and why ADM belongs in them.
prereading.label: AIH C-3

prereading.what: Building a personal currency program, and the optional FAA Form 8710-1 record.
prereading.label: AC 61-98E 1-4 to 1-5

warmup: Your last flight review was signed on the 3rd of a month two years ago. Without looking anything up, on what exact day does it stop letting you act as PIC? And what else in your logbook might already have reset the clock?

key_terms.def: At least 1 hour of ground and 1 hour of flight training with an authorized instructor, covering Part 91 rules and the maneuvers the instructor chooses (14 CFR 61.56).
The flight review stays good through the last day of the 24th calendar month after the month you did it, not to the same date.
A CFI current under 61.197 (ground or flight training), or a ground instructor (ground training only), working within their ratings.
The FAA's voluntary Pilot Proficiency Program. Earning one phase satisfies the flight review requirement.
A set of knowledge and flight activities finished within 12 months. Levels are Basic, Advanced and Master.
FAA Safety Team. Runs FAASafety.gov, WINGS, online courses and safety seminars.
A check by an examiner, approved check airman or U.S. Armed Force for a certificate, rating or operating privilege. Replaces a flight review.
The instructor's written outline of regulatory subjects, maneuvers, sequence and location for the review.
An airborne (altitude, heading, airspace) or ground (runway incursion) violation of ATC or airspace rules.
The last month of a CFI's recent experience period. It goes on endorsements in place of a certificate expiration date.
A debrief where you replay, reconstruct, reflect and redirect, so you assess yourself with the instructor.
Your own plan for regular practice that aims at proficiency beyond the legal minimum.

chunks.title: The rule as it reads now

callout.text: 61.56(c): no person may act as PIC unless, since the beginning of the 24th calendar month before the month of the flight, that person has (1) accomplished a flight review given in an aircraft for which that pilot is rated by an authorized instructor, and (2) a logbook endorsement from the instructor who gave it [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(c)]].

body.p: A flight review is at least 1 hour of flight training and 1 hour of ground training [[60:236|14 CFR 61.56(a)]]. It must include two things [[60:236|14 CFR 61.56(a)]]:

bullets: A review of the current general operating and flight rules of Part 91.
A review of the maneuvers and procedures that the instructor decides you need to show the safe exercise of your certificate's privileges.

body.p: In practice: the rule limits acting as PIC. You may still fly with an instructor or another pilot acting as PIC while your review is out of date [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(c)]]. The review must be in an aircraft you are rated for, but one review covers all your ratings. A pilot with ASEL and balloon ratings can do it in either [[15:24|AC 61-98E 4.2.1.1]].

head: Part of 61.56(c)
What it means for you
rows: 1 hr ground + 1 hr flight minimum, Part 91 rules + instructor's choice of maneuvers [[60:236|14 CFR 61.56(a)]]
Aircraft for which you are rated
Any category and class you hold. Not a multiengine airplane if you have no MEL rating [[15:24|AC 61-98E 4.2.1.1]]
A CFI current under 61.197, within the limits of their ratings [[60:184|14 CFR 61.1(b)]]
From the instructor who gave the review, saying you completed it satisfactorily [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(c)]]

callout.text: Changed: the FAA no longer uses the term "Biennial Flight Review." It implied you only needed training once every 24 calendar months. The FAA wants training as often as you need it, so the name is now just "flight review" [[15:5|AC 61-98E 1.7.1]].

check.q: You hold a private certificate with ASEL and glider ratings. Can a review flown in a glider keep you legal to act as PIC of a Cessna 172?
check.a: Yes. One review in any aircraft you are rated for meets the rule for all of them. The AC still suggests an airplane review if you plan to fly airplanes again soon [[15:24|AC 61-98E 4.2.1.1]] [[15:24|AC 61-98E 4.2.1.2]].

body.p: The window looks back from the month you fly. Find the 24th calendar month before this month. If your review (or other qualifying event) happened on or after the first day of that month, you are good [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(c)]].
The easy way: a review done any day in a month is good through the last day of the same month two years later.

head: Review signed
Good through
First month you are not legal as PIC

callout.text: Common mistake: counting 24 months to the day. The rule counts calendar months, so a review on March 3 is good through the end of March two years later, not March 3 [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(c)]].

body.p: Check every qualifying event, not just the last flight review endorsement. A practical test, a proficiency check or a WINGS phase also starts a new 24 calendar month window [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(d)]] [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(e)]]. Your latest one sets the due date.
A summary form like this one helps. Put your last flight review, its type (certificate, rating or WINGS), and your recent experience in one place [[30:14|RMH 2-2]].

check.q: Your flight review was signed March 31, 2025. You passed your instrument rating practical test with an examiner on June 2, 2026. Through what date may you act as PIC?
check.a: June 30, 2028. The practical test is newer and replaces a flight review, so it starts its own window [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(c)-(d)]].

chunks.title: Who may give it, and the endorsement

body.p: An authorized instructor is a CFI current under 61.197 for ground or flight training, or a ground instructor current under 61.217 for ground training only [[60:184|14 CFR 61.1(b)]]. A CFI's privileges include flight reviews and their endorsements [[60:345|14 CFR 61.193(a)(7)]].

head: Instructor
Flight review privilege
rows: Ground and flight portions, in aircraft that match the CFI's ratings [[60:184|14 CFR 61.1(b)]]
Ground training for a sport, recreational or private pilot flight review [[60:354|14 CFR 61.215]]
Ground training for any flight review except training required for an instrument rating [[60:354|14 CFR 61.215]]

body.p: The instructor must hold category, class and (if needed) type ratings on their pilot certificate, and the matching rating on their instructor certificate. A review in a multiengine airplane needs multiengine ratings on both [[15:25|AC 61-98E 4.2.5]].
A CFI may not endorse your logbook for a flight review unless that CFI actually conducted the review under 61.56(a) [[60:347|14 CFR 61.195(d)(5)]]. A lunch chat about regulations is not a review.

callout.text: Sample endorsement: "I certify that [name], [grade of pilot certificate], [certificate number], has satisfactorily completed a flight review of § 61.56(a) on [date]." Then signature, date, CFI number and RE end date or expiration date [[15:42|AC 61-98E App F]].

Changed: a flight instructor certificate issued on or after December 1, 2024 has no expiration date. One issued before that date still expires 24 calendar months from the month it was issued, renewed or reinstated [[60:203|14 CFR 61.19(d)]]. Instructor privileges now depend on recent experience within the preceding 24 calendar months under 61.197 [[60:351|14 CFR 61.197(a)]]. That is why endorsements show the instructor's recent experience (RE) end date, or a certificate expiration date if there is one [[15:42|AC 61-98E App F Note 2]].

body.p: Log the ground and flight time in your logbook [[60:227|14 CFR 61.51(a)(1)]] [[15:29|AC 61-98E 4.4.2]]. Your instructor may also send an FAA Form 8710-1 so the review goes on your FAA record. This is encouraged but optional [[15:8|AC 61-98E 1.10.2]].

If the review is not satisfactory, the instructor logs it as dual instruction given, not a failure. There is no such thing as failing a flight review in the rule [[15:28|AC 61-98E 4.4.1]] [[15:6|AC 61-98E 1.8.3]].

check.q: Your review was not satisfactory, and your old one runs out in 3 weeks. Can you keep acting as PIC?
check.a: Yes, until the 24 calendar months from your last qualifying event run out. After that you may not act as PIC [[15:29|AC 61-98E 4.4.1]].

chunks.title: What else counts: tests, checks and other exceptions

body.p: You do not need a separate flight review if, inside the same 24 calendar month window, you passed one of these [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(d)]]:

bullets: A pilot proficiency check or practical test by an examiner, an approved pilot check airman or a U.S. Armed Force, for a pilot certificate, rating or operating privilege.
A practical test by an examiner for a flight instructor certificate, an added instructor rating, instructor recent experience under 61.197(b)(1), or reinstatement under 61.199(b)(2).

body.p: So a checkride for a new rating, or a proficiency check given by an approved check airman, resets the clock [[15:23|AC 61-98E 4.1.2.3.1]]. The words "in an aircraft for which that pilot is rated" are in 61.56(c)(1), for the flight review. Paragraph (d) sets no aircraft or class condition for the test or check, so an airline check in a multiengine airplane also covers your single-engine flying [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(c)-(d)]].

head: Paragraph
Who it helps
What it does
rows: One or more WINGS phases replace the flight review [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(e)]]
No flight review while training with a current solo endorsement [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(g)]]
Skip only the 1 hour of ground training if instructor recent experience (61.197) or a FIRC reinstatement was done in the window [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(f)]]
Instructor may combine the review with 61.57 currency, such as an IPC [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(h)]]
A simulator or FTD works only in an approved Part 142 course [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(i)(1)]]

body.p: In a device, the device must represent an aircraft you are rated for. Unless the simulator is approved for landings, you must also meet the 61.57(a) or (b) takeoff and landing rules [[60:238|14 CFR 61.56(i)(2)-(3)]]. An airplane with a single throwover control wheel may be used for a review if the conditions of 91.109(b) are met [[60:446|14 CFR 91.109(b)]].

callout.text: Common mistake: thinking an IPC from a CFI, a club checkout or three landings in 90 days replaces a flight review. None of them is on the 61.56(d) or (e) list [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(d)]]. If you want an IPC and a review together, ask the instructor to combine them [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(h)]].

A check or test keeps you legal, but the AC suggests a review in the aircraft you will actually fly if your recent flying was in something else and your window is nearly up [[15:23|AC 61-98E 4.1.2.3.2]].

check.q: A CFI renewed her recent experience under 61.197 last year. What is the minimum flight review she needs now?
check.a: 1 hour of flight training. She may skip the 1 hour of ground training [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(f)]].

body.p: WINGS is the FAA's voluntary program built around the leading causes of GA accidents, such as poor decision making, performance and limitations, preflight planning, aircraft control and takeoffs and landings [[14:2|AC 61-91K 6]]. Any pilot with an FAA certificate and any required medical may join, including student pilots [[14:2|AC 61-91K 7.1]].

callout.text: 61.56(e): a person who has, within the 24 calendar month window, satisfactorily accomplished one or more phases of an FAA-sponsored pilot proficiency program need not accomplish the flight review [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(e)]].

body.p: Each new phase satisfies the flight review requirement, however close together the phases are [[14:3|AC 61-91K 7.2]]. Any phase at any level counts [[14:5|AC 61-91K 8.4.4]].

head: WINGS fact
Detail
rows: Basic (based on Private ACS), Advanced (commercial standards), Master (ATP, commercial with instrument or CFI standards) [[14:4|AC 61-91K 8.4.1]]
Phase 1 at Basic first, then Advanced. Master needs at least one Advanced phase [[14:5|AC 61-91K 8.4.2-8.4.3]]
All tasks for a phase within 12 months [[14:3|AC 61-91K 7.3.1]]
A Basic phase at least once every 12 months [[14:5|AC 61-91K 8.4.2]]
Online courses (automatic credit) or FAASTeam seminars where you sign the roster [[14:4|AC 61-91K 8.2]]
Flown with a qualified instructor who verifies you met the standard [[14:4|AC 61-91K 8.3.1]]

callout.text: Common mistake: thinking WINGS flight review credit lasts only 12 months. The AC says you must finish a phase's tasks within 12 months, and that a phase is then "valid for 12 months" as a WINGS phase [[14:3|AC 61-91K 7.3.1]]. For the flight review, the rule counts a phase for the full 24 calendar month window of 61.56(c) [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(e)]] [[14:3|AC 61-91K 7.2]].

body.p: When you sign a seminar roster, use the same email as your FAASafety.gov account, or the credit won't reach you [[14:4|AC 61-91K 8.2.2]]. Your record and a wallet-sized flight review certificate are on your My WINGS page [[14:5|AC 61-91K 8.4.4]]. An instructor may also endorse your logbook for a completed phase, but that endorsement is not required [[14:7|AC 61-91K 8.9 Note]].

callout.text: Changed: AC 61-91K (October 2024) replaced AC 61-91J, and the program is now the "WINGS-Pilot Proficiency Program" [[14:1|AC 61-91K 4]]. Some older handbooks still call it an "awards" program [[24:28|AFH 1-7]].

check.q: You finished Basic Phase 1 in June 2025 and Basic Phase 2 in March 2026. Through what date is your flight review requirement met?
check.a: March 31, 2028. Each new phase satisfies 61.56, so the newest one sets the window [[14:3|AC 61-91K 7.2]] [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(c)]].

chunks.title: What the review covers: Part 91 on the ground

body.p: The ground review must cover the current general operating and flight rules of Part 91 [[60:236|14 CFR 61.56(a)]]. The instructor tailors it: broad enough that you can comply with all the rules in all kinds of airspace and weather, and deeper where your knowledge is weak [[15:26|AC 61-98E 4.3.1]].

Before planning, a good instructor interviews you: what you fly, the kind of flying you do, and how much and how recently you have flown [[15:23|AC 61-98E 4.2]] [[15:24|AC 61-98E 4.2.2]] [[15:25|AC 61-98E 4.2.3]]. If you will start using Class B airspace, Class B rules belong in your review [[15:24|AC 61-98E 4.2.2]].

head: AC 61-98E review area
Sample rules
rows: 61.57 recent experience; 91.3 authority; 91.103 preflight action; 91.17 alcohol or drugs; 91.211 oxygen
91.7 airworthiness; 91.205 equipment; 91.213 inoperative equipment; 91.409 inspections; 91.411 and 91.413 checks
Airport markings and patterns (91.126); airspace (91.129 to 91.135); minimum altitudes (91.119); right-of-way (91.113); speed limits (91.117)
Personal minimums worksheet; 3-P risk management; ACS or PTS

body.p: The table follows the AC's regulatory review guide [[15:40|AC 61-98E App E]] [[15:41|AC 61-98E App E side 2]] and the ground review side of its sample checklist, which groups the rules under pilot, aircraft, environment and external pressure [[15:43|AC 61-98E App F side 2]].

Expect time on pilot deviations. Airborne ones are altitude and heading busts and airspace violations. Ground ones are runway incursions. For many pilots the review is the only regular recurrent training, so the AC asks instructors to stress this [[15:26|AC 61-98E 4.3.2]].

callout.text: Do your 91.103 homework before you show up: weather, runway lengths, weight and balance, a flight log and a flight plan. The instructor may ask for all of it [[15:27|AC 61-98E 4.3.5.2]].

check.q: Name two of the four review areas in the AC's Part 91 ground review guide.
check.a: Any two of pilot, aircraft, environment and external pressure [[15:40|AC 61-98E App E]] [[15:43|AC 61-98E App F side 2]].

chunks.title: What the review covers: maneuvers in the air

body.p: The instructor picks the maneuvers. You should be able to fly all of them to the ACS or PTS standard for the certificate you hold. Abnormal and emergency procedures should always be included [[15:27|AC 61-98E 4.3.5.1]].
Whatever your experience, the instructor should review at least these maneuvers, which are critical to safe flight [[15:28|AC 61-98E 4.3.5.4]]:

bullets: Takeoffs, and stabilized approaches to landings
Stall recognition, stalls and stall recovery
Flight by sole reference to instruments, actual or simulated

body.p: Why takeoffs and landings first? About 80 percent of accidents involve human factors, and most happen in landing (24.1 percent) and takeoff (23.4 percent), a small part of total flight time [[1:41|PHAK 2-2]].
On a stabilized approach the aiming point seems to stay still in the windshield. Touchdown happens farther down the runway because of the distance flown in the flare [[24:176|AFH 9-5]].

Loss of control is the number one root cause of GA fatalities. More than 25 percent of fatal accidents happen while maneuvering, and half of those involve stall/spin [[15:26|AC 61-98E 4.3.4]]. If your airplane has an AOA indicator, the instructor should check that you use and read it correctly. If not, expect questions on AOA basics [[15:27|AC 61-98E 4.3.4]].

In an airplane with automation, the instructor should evaluate your automation competency [[15:26|AC 61-98E 4.3.3]]. The review can be a realistic scenario, like a cross-country with maneuvers along the way [[15:27|AC 61-98E 4.3.5.2]] [[15:28|AC 61-98E 4.3.5.5]].

check.q: Which two phases of flight together hold almost half of GA accidents in PHAK Figure 2-1?
check.a: Landing (24.1 percent) and takeoff/initial climb (23.4 percent), 47.5 percent together [[1:41|PHAK 2-2]].

chunks.title: Fly it step by step: your flight review

body.p: The AC's sample checklist runs the review in five steps [[15:42|AC 61-98E App F]]. Here is what each one means for you.

head: Step
What happens
Your job
rows: Your aeronautical history, expectations, Part 91 and cross-country assignments
Bring your logbook and be honest about weak areas [[15:39|AC 61-98E App D]]
Language standard, regulations, your flight plan, weather, risk management and personal minimums, GA security
Know the rules for the airspace you really use [[15:42|AC 61-98E App F]]
Basic skills, systems and automation, takeoffs and landings, slow flight, stalls, unusual attitudes, power loss, instruments, ADM
Fly to your certificate's ACS standard [[15:27|AC 61-98E 4.3.5.1]]
Replay, reflect, reconstruct, redirect, and questions
Personal minimums worksheet, practice plan, training plan if wanted
Leave with a plan, not just a signature [[15:42|AC 61-98E App F]]

body.p: The review is a training event, not a practical test. The instructor may teach weak areas on the spot. If you fix them, you can still complete the review [[15:22|AC 61-98E 4.1.1]] [[15:28|AC 61-98E 4.3.5.6]].
The 1 hour plus 1 hour is a floor. The instructor decides the total time, and a review may need more [[15:22|AC 61-98E 4.1.1]].

Afterward, check your logbook: the endorsement wording, the instructor's signature, CFI number and RE end date, and the logged ground and flight time [[15:42|AC 61-98E App F]] [[60:227|14 CFR 61.51(a)(1)]].

check.q: In the postflight step, what are the four Rs of a collaborative critique?

chunks.title: Risk: a box to tick or a real check?

body.p: The danger is treating the review as a sign-off every two years. The rule sets a minimum. Many pilots go further and keep current through WINGS all year [[24:37|AFH 1-16]].

Knowledge fades between reviews. One study found that pilots' memory of regulations was linked to how many months had passed since their last flight review. Pilots sharpen up before a review and then let it fade [[25:92|AIH 3-41]].
Familiar airplanes breed complacency. The AIH warns that a pilot getting a review in a familiar aircraft may be prone to it [[25:18|AIH 1-14]].
Being current is not the same as being proficient. Legal currency doesn't prove you can handle the flight you are planning [[30:23|RMH 3-5]].

Use the 3P model in the review and on every flight: perceive the hazards, process the risk, perform the change [[30:55|RMH 8-2]]. Instructors should stress risk management in every recurrent event, and use scenarios that mirror how you really fly [[25:189|AIH 10-5]].

callout.text: Build a personal currency program that aims past the minimum [[15:7|AC 61-98E 1.9.1]]. The AC's sample practice plan has a VFR profile every 4 to 6 weeks: steep turns, stalls, slow flight, short- and soft-field landings, then a self-review [[15:37|AC 61-98E App B]].

check.q: Your review is current, but you have flown 4 hours this year. Does the rule say you are ready for a night trip with passengers?
check.a: The flight review rule only makes you legal to act as PIC. Proficiency is a separate question, so practice or get training first [[30:23|RMH 3-5]] [[15:7|AC 61-98E 1.9.1]]. Night passengers also need 61.57(b) night currency [[60:238|14 CFR 61.57(b)]].

bullets: Counting the 24 months to the day instead of to the end of the month [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(c)]].
Missing a newer checkride, proficiency check or WINGS phase that already reset the clock [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(d)]] [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(e)]].
Flying the review in an aircraft you are not rated for, such as a twin without an MEL rating [[15:24|AC 61-98E 4.2.1.1]].
Assuming an IPC from a CFI, a club checkout or 90-day landings replace the review [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(d)]].
An endorsement signed by someone who did not give the review [[60:347|14 CFR 61.195(d)(5)]].
Planning a review around the 1 plus 1 hour minimum [[15:22|AC 61-98E 4.1.2]].
Signing a WINGS seminar roster with a different email, or never asking the instructor to validate flight activities [[14:4|AC 61-91K 8.2.2]] [[14:4|AC 61-91K 8.3.1]].
Mixing up passenger currency: a review in one class doesn't give you 61.57 landings in another [[60:238|14 CFR 61.57(a)]].

check.q: Your logbook shows a review signed by a CFI friend who never flew with you. Is it valid?
check.a: No. A CFI may not endorse a flight review unless they conducted it under 61.56(a) [[60:347|14 CFR 61.195(d)(5)]].

scenario.title: "Just give me the quickest BFR"
scenario.setup: It is October 20, 2026. Marco is a private pilot with 220 hours who flies about 20 hours a year from a small nontowered field. His last flight review was signed November 12, 2024. He just bought a used airplane with a glass panel and an autopilot, and next month he wants to start flying into a nearby Class B airport for work. He calls his CFI: "I just need the quickest BFR possible. One hour on the ground, one in the air, sign me off."

questions.q: Through what date may Marco act as PIC on his current review?
questions.a: November 30, 2026. A review in November 2024 is good through the end of November two years later [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(c)]].

questions.q: What is wrong with asking for "the quickest BFR"?
questions.a: The FAA dropped "biennial" because it suggested training only every 24 months [[15:5|AC 61-98E 1.7.1]]. The 1 plus 1 hour is a minimum, and the instructor plans for proficiency, not the minimum [[15:22|AC 61-98E 4.1.1]] [[15:22|AC 61-98E 4.1.2]].

questions.q: What should the Part 91 ground review stress for Marco?
questions.a: Class B rules and procedures, because his flying is about to change [[15:24|AC 61-98E 4.2.2]], plus pilot deviation avoidance [[15:26|AC 61-98E 4.3.2]]. Class B also means equipment rules such as Mode C and ADS-B [[25:189|AIH 10-5]].

questions.q: What should the flight portion include besides the basic maneuvers?
questions.a: His new airplane's systems, performance and automation [[15:25|AC 61-98E 4.2.3]] [[15:26|AC 61-98E 4.3.3]], abnormal and emergency procedures [[15:27|AC 61-98E 4.3.5.1]], and the critical maneuvers such as stalls and stabilized approaches [[15:28|AC 61-98E 4.3.5.4]]. A glass-panel transition calls for specialized training from an instructor who knows that equipment [[15:26|AC 61-98E 4.3.3]].

questions.q: After two hours he is not yet up to standard. What happens?
questions.a: The instructor logs dual instruction given, not a failure, uses the ACS to debrief, and recommends more training [[15:28|AC 61-98E 4.4.1]] [[15:29|AC 61-98E 4.4.1]]. Marco may still act as PIC through November 30, but not after that without a completed review [[15:29|AC 61-98E 4.4.1]].

questions.q: How can Marco avoid the end-of-window rush next time?
questions.a: Join WINGS: each phase he earns satisfies the flight review, however often he does them [[14:3|AC 61-91K 7.2]]. Add a personal practice plan, like a proficiency flight every 4 to 6 weeks [[15:7|AC 61-98E 1.9.1]] [[15:37|AC 61-98E App B]].

skills.do: From a logbook, find every qualifying event (flight review endorsement, practical test or proficiency check, WINGS phase), check that each one is valid (rated aircraft, right instructor, proper endorsement), and state the last day you may act as PIC.
skills.practice: Audit your own logbook. Write your newest qualifying event and its due date in a summary like RMH Figure 2-2 [[30:14|RMH 2-2]]. Count to the end of the 24th calendar month [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(c)]], and check the endorsement items against the AC's sample [[15:42|AC 61-98E App F]].

quiz.q: What is the minimum training for a standard airplane flight review?
options: 1 hour total, ground and flight combined
2 hours of flight training only, with no ground training required
1 hour of ground and 1 hour of flight training
3 takeoffs and landings plus an oral exam
quiz.why: 61.56(a) requires at least 1 hour of flight training and 1 hour of ground training [[60:236|14 CFR 61.56(a)]].

quiz.q: Your flight review was signed January 9, 2025. What is the last day you may act as PIC on it?
options: January 9, 2027
January 31, 2027
December 31, 2026
February 28, 2027
quiz.why: The window runs from the beginning of the 24th calendar month before the flight month. For January 2027 that is January 2025, so the review counts all of January 2027 [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(c)]].

quiz.q: Who decides which maneuvers you fly on a flight review?
options: The FAA, from a fixed list in Part 61
Your aircraft's insurance company
You, as long as you fly at least three
The instructor giving the review
quiz.why: 61.56(a)(2) leaves the maneuvers and procedures to the discretion of the person giving the review [[60:236|14 CFR 61.56(a)]].

quiz.q: Which event replaces a flight review?
options: Passing a practical test with an examiner for a new rating
A checkout in a new rental airplane given by the rental operator's chief pilot
Three takeoffs and landings made within the previous 90 days with a passenger aboard
An instrument proficiency check given by a CFI to restore instrument currency
quiz.why: A practical test by an examiner for a certificate, rating or operating privilege is on the 61.56(d) list. The others are not [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(d)]].

quiz.q: You earned WINGS phases in February and in September of the same year. How does that affect your flight review?
options: Only the first phase counts; the second must wait 24 months
The September phase starts a new 24 calendar month window
Neither counts unless a CFI endorses your logbook
WINGS only counts for 12 months after each phase
quiz.why: Each new phase satisfies the flight review requirement, however closely spaced [[14:3|AC 61-91K 7.2]]. The logbook endorsement for a phase is optional [[14:7|AC 61-91K 8.9 Note]].

quiz.q: How are WINGS flight activities credited?
options: They are credited when you sign a seminar roster
You log them yourself on FAASafety.gov
A qualified instructor verifies you flew them to standard
An FAA inspector must watch the flight
quiz.why: Flying tasks are done with a qualified instructor who verifies the standard was met [[14:4|AC 61-91K 8.3.1]].

quiz.q: Your flight review is not satisfactory. How should the instructor log it?
options: As a failed flight review
As an unsatisfactory review with the reasons
Nothing is logged at all
As dual instruction given
quiz.why: The FAA does not intend the review to be a practical test. It is logged as dual instruction given, not a failure [[15:28|AC 61-98E 4.4.1]].

quiz.q: Your airplane has no AOA indicator. What does AC 61-98E ask the instructor to do?
options: Skip all AOA topics
Stress AOA and check your general AOA knowledge
Use only the stall warning horn as the AOA reference
Require an AOA indicator before the review
quiz.why: Without an AOA indicator, the instructor should emphasize its importance and evaluate your general knowledge of AOA aerodynamics [[15:27|AC 61-98E 4.3.4]].

quiz.q: You want to do your flight review in a flight training device. What is required?
options: An approved course at a Part 142 training center
Any FTD, as long as a CFI is present and the device represents your aircraft
A basic aviation training device at your flying club with a CFI running the session
Written FSDO approval for each review that is flown in a simulator or FTD
quiz.why: A simulator or FTD may be used only in an approved course at a Part 142 training center [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(i)(1)]].

takeaways: No flight review, test, check or WINGS phase in the window means you may not act as PIC.
Good through the end of the 24th calendar month: March 3 is good to the end of March two years later.
Practical tests, proficiency checks and WINGS phases all reset the clock. A CFI's IPC or a checkout does not.
1 hour ground + 1 hour flight is the floor. Part 91 rules + instructor's choice of maneuvers, to your ACS standard.
Only the instructor who gave the review endorses it. Not satisfactory = dual given, never a failure.
Use WINGS and a personal practice plan so the review checks proficiency instead of creating it.
cfi_notes: AC 61-98E 4.1.1 says the 1 plus 1 hour applies except under 61.56(b), (d) and (e). The rule itself says (b) and (f), with (f) letting some CFIs skip the ground hour [[15:22|AC 61-98E 4.1.1]] [[60:236|14 CFR 61.56(a)]]. Teach the rule.

AC 61-98E 4.1.2.1 says "within the preceding 24 calendar months." Teach the rule's words, "since the beginning of the 24th calendar month before the month," and drill end-of-month examples [[15:23|AC 61-98E 4.1.2.1]] [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(c)]].

Outdated names: AC 61-98E App F and AC 61-91K 7.2 still quote a pilot proficiency "award" program, and AFH 1-7 says "Pilot Proficiency Awards Wings Program." Current 61.56(e) reads "FAA-sponsored pilot proficiency program" [[15:42|AC 61-98E App F]] [[24:28|AFH 1-7]] [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(e)]].

Airline and other professional pilots often meet 61.56 through a check airman's proficiency check [[15:23|AC 61-98E 4.1.2.3.1]]. Remind them that 61.57(a) landings are by category and class, and suggest a review in the light airplane they will fly [[15:23|AC 61-98E 4.1.2.3.2]] [[60:238|14 CFR 61.57(a)]].
Start with the AC's interview (Appendix D) and build the plan around how the pilot really flies. Scenarios should mirror that profile [[15:39|AC 61-98E App D]] [[25:189|AIH 10-5]].
Watch for complacency in pilots flying a familiar airplane, and for knowledge crammed just before the review [[25:18|AIH 1-14]] [[25:92|AIH 3-41]].
If the review is unsatisfactory, use the ACS as the objective standard in the debrief and offer a practical plan of ground and flight training [[15:28|AC 61-98E 4.4.1]] [[15:29|AC 61-98E 4.4.1]].
Don't take a review in an airplane you are not current or familiar with. Decline and refer the pilot rather than fake it [[15:19|AC 61-98E 2.4.1]] [[15:25|AC 61-98E 4.2.5]].
gaps: The exact current WINGS phase requirements (number and topics of knowledge and flight activities) are only on FAASafety.gov. AC 61-91K describes them in general terms.
AC 61-65 (the official endorsement samples) is not in the sources. Endorsement wording here comes from AC 61-98E Appendix F and AC 61-91K 8.8 to 8.9.
The sources do not say whether an IPC given by an examiner (not a CFI) counts as a 61.56(d)(1) proficiency check. No FAA legal interpretations are uploaded.
Details of approved Part 142 flight review courses in simulators are not in the sources.
Glider (61.56(b)) and type-specific rules (Robinson R-22/R-44 SFAR, MU-2B) are only noted, not taught.

activities.title: When is it due?
activities.intro: Work it out, then type your answer. Type a year and month as six digits, for example 202703 for March 2027.

items.q: Your flight review was endorsed May 14, 2025. Nothing else has happened since. What is the last month you may act as PIC? (YYYYMM)
items.why: For May 2027, the 24th calendar month before is May 2025, and May 14 falls after May 1. For June 2027 it would be June 2025, which is after the review. So May 2027 [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(c)]].

items.q: Last flight review: February 2, 2025. You completed a WINGS phase on November 20, 2025. Last month you may act as PIC? (YYYYMM)
items.why: The WINGS phase is newer and replaces the review [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(e)]]. November 2025 plus 24 calendar months is good through November 2027 [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(c)]].

items.q: Last flight review: June 2024. You passed your commercial practical test with an examiner on January 30, 2026. Last month you may act as PIC? (YYYYMM)
items.why: A practical test by an examiner replaces the flight review [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(d)]]. January 2026 is good through January 2028 [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(c)]].

items.q: Your review was signed October 31, 2024. What is the last day of October 2026 on which you may act as PIC? Type the day.
items.why: For October 2026 the window starts October 1, 2024, and the review is after that, so all of October counts, through the 31st. On November 1 the window starts November 1, 2024, and the review no longer counts [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(c)]].

items.q: A CFI who completed her 61.197 recent experience last year needs a flight review. What is the minimum total hours of ground plus flight training?
items.why: Normally 1 + 1 = 2 hours [[60:236|14 CFR 61.56(a)]], but 61.56(f) waives the 1 hour of ground training for her, leaving 1 hour of flight training [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(f)]].

activities.title: Who signs, and what gets logged
activities.intro: Decide if each statement is true or false.

cards.s: A ground instructor can give the whole flight review, ground and flight.
cards.why: No. A ground instructor is an authorized instructor only for ground training [[60:184|14 CFR 61.1(b)]] [[60:354|14 CFR 61.215]].

cards.s: A CFI may endorse a flight review only if that CFI conducted it under 61.56(a).
cards.why: Yes. 61.195(d)(5) bars endorsing a review the instructor did not conduct [[60:347|14 CFR 61.195(d)(5)]].

cards.s: When a review is unsatisfactory, the instructor must write the failure in your logbook.
cards.why: No. No logbook entry showing unsatisfactory performance is required. The flight is logged as dual given [[15:42|AC 61-98E App F Note 1]] [[15:28|AC 61-98E 4.4.1]].

cards.s: Sending FAA Form 8710-1 after a flight review is required.
cards.why: No. The FAA strongly encourages it, but it is optional [[15:8|AC 61-98E 1.10.2]].

cards.s: To give a review in a multiengine airplane, a CFI needs multiengine ratings on both the pilot and instructor certificates.
The ground and flight time from your review must be logged in your logbook.
cards.why: Yes. Training used for a flight review must be recorded [[60:227|14 CFR 61.51(a)(1)]] [[15:29|AC 61-98E 4.4.2]].

activities.title: Does it meet 61.56?
activities.intro: Tap a clue, then tap where it belongs.
buckets: Does not replace a flight review

items.t: Passed an instrument rating practical test with an examiner
Airline proficiency check with an approved check airman
Completed a WINGS phase at any level
Student pilot in training with a current solo endorsement
Instrument proficiency check given by a CFI
Three takeoffs and landings in the last 90 days
Club checkout in a new rental airplane
A CFI's 61.197 renewal (it only waives the ground hour)

activities.why: 61.56(d) lists practical tests and proficiency checks by examiners, check airmen or the Armed Forces; (e) WINGS; (g) student pilots [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(d)]] [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(e)]] [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(g)]]. A CFI renewal only waives the ground hour [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(f)]].

activities.title: Read the AOA picture
activities.intro: Drag each name to its numbered pin.

pins.label: Wing at normal AOA, smooth flow

activities.why: A stall happens when smooth airflow is disrupted because the AOA exceeds the critical AOA [[24:117|AFH 5-12]]. An AOA indicator shows how close you are to the critical AOA [[24:118|AFH 5-13]], and a flight review should check that you read it correctly [[15:27|AC 61-98E 4.3.4]].

activities.title: Run the review in order
activities.intro: Use the arrows to put the steps in order, then tap Check.
steps: Interview: your aeronautical history, type of flying and goals
Agree on the plan and standards; get your Part 91 and cross-country assignments
Ground review: rules, your flight plan, weather, risk and personal minimums
Flight: basic skills, takeoffs and landings, slow flight, stalls, emergencies, instruments
Improvement plan: personal minimums and a proficiency practice plan
activities.why: These follow the five steps of the AC's sample flight review checklist [[15:42|AC 61-98E App F]] and the pre-review agreement [[15:25|AC 61-98E 4.2.4]].

activities.title: Can I take my sister flying Saturday?
activities.intro: It is Monday, October 5. You fly as an airline first officer and hold an ATP certificate that also lets you fly single-engine land airplanes. Your last airline proficiency check, with an approved check airman, was in May. Your last flight review in a light single was in 2022, and your last single-engine landing was two years ago. On Saturday you want to rent the club's Cessna 172 and take your sister on a local VFR flight.

steps.s: First question: are you legal on the flight review?
options: No: you need a flight review in a single-engine airplane before you can act as PIC
Only if the check was flown in a single-engine airplane, which is what you will fly
Yes: the proficiency check by an approved check airman meets 61.56
Only for 12 months after the check, then a flight review is due again
steps.why: 61.56(d)(1) lists "a pilot proficiency check ... conducted by ... an approved pilot check airman ... for a pilot certificate, rating, or operating privilege" [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(d)]] [[15:23|AC 61-98E 4.1.2.3.1]]. The words "in an aircraft for which that pilot is rated" are only in 61.56(c)(1), for the flight review itself. Paragraph (d) sets no aircraft, category or class condition, so a check flown in a multiengine airplane still meets the rule for your single-engine flying [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(c)-(d)]].

steps.s: Next: can you carry your sister?
options: Yes: your airline landings in the last 90 days keep you current as pilot in command
Yes: no landing currency is needed for a local day VFR flight with one passenger
Not yet: you need 3 night full-stop landings in a single-engine land airplane first
Not yet: you need 3 takeoffs and landings in a single-engine land airplane in 90 days
steps.why: To carry passengers you need 3 takeoffs and landings in the last 90 days in the same category and class, as sole manipulator of the controls [[60:238|14 CFR 61.57(a)]]. Your airline landings are in a different class.

steps.s: The flight review is covered, but you still need 3 landings in a single and have not flown one in two years. How do you prepare for Saturday?
options: Book a CFI flight on takeoffs, stabilized approaches, slow flight, stalls and emergencies in the 172
Fly 3 solo landings Friday and go Saturday, with no other practice or instructor review
Skip extra practice; airline flying keeps every skill sharp, including slow flight and stalls
Ask the club to waive its checkout and rely on your airline experience instead
steps.why: The AC suggests a review in the aircraft you will fly when your recent flying was in something else [[15:23|AC 61-98E 4.1.2.3.2]], covering the critical maneuvers [[15:28|AC 61-98E 4.3.5.4]]. Familiar skills fade with disuse [[25:92|AIH 3-41]].

steps.s: On the CFI flight you float long on two of three landings. The CFI suggests another session. What now?
options: Go Saturday anyway, since you are legal on currency and the CFI's advice is optional
Fly a second session before Saturday, making sure you get 3 landings as sole manipulator
Insist on a flight review endorsement to prove to the club that you are fine
Switch to a different instructor who will sign you off after one quick flight
steps.why: The goal is proficiency: the instructor may add training until weak areas are fixed [[15:28|AC 61-98E 4.3.5.6]]. Landings with the CFI count for 61.57 if you were sole manipulator [[60:238|14 CFR 61.57(a)]].

steps.s: You want to stay sharp in light airplanes without waiting for problems. What is a good plan?
options: Fly one flight review every 24 calendar months
Rely on your airline checks only
Wait until the club requires a new checkout
Join WINGS and earn phases with an instructor
steps.why: WINGS gives you regular flight activities with an instructor, and each phase also meets the flight review rule [[14:3|AC 61-91K 7.2]] [[14:4|AC 61-91K 8.3.1]]. The FAA strongly encourages it [[15:7|AC 61-98E 1.9.2]].

final_quiz.q: Your flight review was signed March 3, 2025. Today is April 2, 2027, and you want to fly solo. Are you legal as PIC?
options: No, it ran out at the end of March 2027
Yes, it is good until March 3, 2029
Yes, a solo flight needs no flight review
No, it ran out on March 3, 2027
final_quiz.why: A March 2025 review is good through March 31, 2027. For April 2027 the window starts April 1, 2025 [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(c)]]. The rule applies to any PIC flight, solo or not.

final_quiz.q: You hold only an ASEL rating. You fly a flight review with a CFI in a light twin. Does it count?
options: Yes, any airplane counts toward a flight review for an ASEL pilot
Yes, if the CFI holds a multiengine rating and acts as PIC for the flight
No, it must be in an aircraft you are rated for
No, flight reviews must be flown in a Cessna 172 or a similar single-engine trainer
final_quiz.why: The review must be in an aircraft for which you are rated, so a twin without an MEL rating doesn't count [[15:24|AC 61-98E 4.2.1.1]] [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(c)]].

final_quiz.q: A student pilot has a current solo endorsement and has been training for 30 months. Does she need a flight review to fly solo?
options: Yes, before any cross-country flight once she passes 24 months of training
Yes, every 24 calendar months, the same as for a certificated pilot
No, not while training with a current solo endorsement
Only if she is over 40 or has logged more than 100 hours of training
final_quiz.why: 61.56(g) exempts a student pilot who is training for a certificate and holds a current solo endorsement [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(g)]].

final_quiz.q: Your club's airplane has one throwover control wheel. Under 91.109(b), how many hours of PIC time in that make and model must the instructor have to give a flight review in it?
final_quiz.why: The instructor must be current and qualified as PIC, meet 61.195(b), and have at least 25 hours of PIC time in the make and model [[60:446|14 CFR 91.109(b)]].

final_quiz.q: An advanced ground instructor offers to do your private pilot flight review. What can she do?
options: The whole review, ground and flight
Nothing, ground instructors can't help with reviews
Only the ground training portion
Only the endorsement
final_quiz.why: An AGI may give the ground training for any flight review except instrument-rating training [[60:354|14 CFR 61.215]]. The flight portion needs a CFI [[60:184|14 CFR 61.1(b)]].

final_quiz.q: You want to start earning Advanced WINGS phases. What must you have done first?
options: Phase 1 at the Basic level
A commercial pilot certificate
A current IPC
A Master level phase
final_quiz.why: All participants must finish Phase 1 at the Basic level before getting credit for more phases or moving up [[14:5|AC 61-91K 8.4.2]].

final_quiz.q: You did a WINGS online course 14 months ago and two flight activities this month. What does AC 61-91K say about that set?
options: All tasks for a phase must be done within 12 months, so the old course won't count toward it
Any tasks done within the last 24 months can be combined to make a phase
Online courses never count toward any phase; only seminars and flight activities do
A phase needs only flight activities, so the online course is not part of it at all
final_quiz.why: All the tasks for a phase must be completed within a 12-month period [[14:3|AC 61-91K 7.3.1]].

final_quiz.q: Your new CFI got her certificate in 2025. What goes on your flight review endorsement instead of a certificate expiration date?
options: Nothing, no dates are needed
Her medical certificate date
Her recent experience (RE) end date
Her FAASTeam number
final_quiz.why: Instructor certificates issued on or after December 1, 2024 have no expiration [[60:203|14 CFR 61.19(d)]]. Endorsements show the RE end date [[15:42|AC 61-98E App F Note 2]].

final_quiz.q: You are due for both an IPC and a flight review. What do the rules allow?
options: They must be done on separate days
Only an examiner can do both
The IPC automatically replaces the review
The instructor may combine them
final_quiz.why: 61.56(h) lets the instructor combine the review with 61.57 requirements, such as an IPC [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(h)]]. An IPC by itself is not on the replacement list [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(d)]].

final_quiz.q: In PHAK Figure 2-1, takeoff/initial climb and landing together account for what share of GA accidents?
options: 24.1 percent
47.5 percent
33.8 percent
15.7 percent
final_quiz.why: Takeoff 23.4 percent plus landing 24.1 percent is 47.5 percent [[1:41|PHAK 2-2]].

final_quiz.q: You fly mostly locally, but next month you will start flying into Class B airspace. What should your instructor do in the review?
options: Use the same plan as for any pilot, since the review does not depend on your flying
Skip airspace and focus on landings, since those are the most common accident phase
Send you to an examiner instead, because Class B needs a new practical test
Include Class B requirements and procedures
final_quiz.why: When your flying is about to change, the review should cover the new area, such as Class B operating requirements [[15:24|AC 61-98E 4.2.2]] [[25:189|AIH 10-5]].

final_quiz.q: You are two hours into your review and still weak on stalls. The instructor teaches them, and you then fly them to standard. Can the review still be completed?
options: No, any weak area noted during the review means the whole review is a failure
No, you must wait 30 days and then repeat the entire review from the start
Yes, but only with an examiner present to witness the extra instruction
Yes, extra instruction doesn't block completion if you correct the weak areas
final_quiz.why: The instructor may teach weak areas during the review, and that does not prevent completion as long as they are corrected [[15:28|AC 61-98E 4.3.5.6]].

final_quiz.q: What does AC 61-98E say about sending FAA Form 8710-1 after a flight review?
options: It is required within 7 days
It is optional but strongly encouraged
It is required only for WINGS
It is not allowed for flight reviews
final_quiz.why: The FAA does not require it but strongly encourages it, so your FAA record stays current [[15:8|AC 61-98E 1.10.2]].
